newsitem.title: KENYA: Congestion hits Kenya's Mombasa port.
newsitem.headline: Congestion hits Kenya's Mombasa port.

text.p: Congestion at Mombasa's container terminal was reported on Tuesday as three ships waited to unload.
But Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) officials said conditions were better than on Friday when up to seven ships were waiting.
They blamed the congestion on a go-slow last week by KPA drivers, crane operators and other employees in a dispute with management over salaries.
KPA workers have demanded an 80 percent increase. They say senior managers have been awarded two increases this year alone.
The container terminal is managed by British company Felixstowe Port Consultants, who declined comment on the dispute.
The Daily Nation newspaper reported on Tuesday that the Dockworkers' Union had issued a 21-day strike notice after the ports management refused to increase salaries.
The go-slow ended after a week but no one knows whether the salaries question will be reviewed.
Since Felixtowe took over management in September, local staff have complained of a wide gap in salaries between them and five expatriates who were brought in.
Such disparities exist in many companies in Kenya.
The KPA said MV MSC Sariska which arrived on November 20, MV Vigilant which arrived on November 21, and MV Umofolozi which arrived on November 23 were waiting for berthing space.
Berth five at the conventional terminal was still out of use for crane repair while numbers 11 and 12 were closed indefinitely for quayside repairs.
The KPA said 33 ships with an assortment of 56,455 tonnes of cargo were expected in the next two weeks.
KPA authorities feared that if the go-slow continued, congestion would mount.
